title: Chunking and Indexing Documents
summary: Documents are split into chunks before they are embedded, and the split decides what the retriever can find. This lesson works out chunk counts, overlap overhead, the chance a fact is cut in half, index size, and how structure-aware and parent-child chunking help.
objectives: Explain why whole documents are not embedded as a single vector and why chunk size is a trade-off
Compute chunk count with ceil((L − o)/(s − o)) and the overlap overhead s/(s − o)
Compute the probability that a fact of f tokens is split by a chunk boundary and how overlap reduces it
Compute index size N · d · bytes and indexing cost for a collection
Choose between fixed-size, sentence, heading-aware and parent-child chunking, and evaluate the choice with labelled questions
prerequisites: You should know the offline indexing pipeline from [How RAG Works](/learn/retrieval-and-rag/rag-architecture), how dense retrieval embeds text ([Term-Based and Embedding Retrieval](/learn/retrieval-and-rag/sparse-and-dense)), and the retrieval metrics from [Hybrid Search and Reranking](/learn/retrieval-and-rag/hybrid-and-reranking).
